I'll speak as this farmer and then give my plan as JSON.

**My reasoning:**

I farm 6 mu with my family. My main money comes from garlic — Quzhou garlic sells well, the dealers come to the village every summer to buy. So I put 4 mu in garlic this autumn, and keep 2 mu for wheat because we eat our own flour, I don't like buying noodles from the market. After I pull up the garlic in May and cut the wheat in June, I plant summer maize on all 6 mu — the maize is for feeding and some for selling.

For garlic, I do like last year because last year the price was good and I got maybe 2000 jin per mu. I buy the compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) before planting — about 4 bags per mu, that is 200 jin. Then when the garlic comes up in spring I top-dress with urea, 1 bag per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang's wife said she cut the fertilizer and her garlic was small, so I would rather use a bit more. Garlic also needs water — I irrigate once before the ground freezes, once when the shoots come out in spring, then two or three more times when the bulbs swell. For pests I spray maybe 4 times — leaf disease, thrips, and the maggots in the bulb.

For wheat, I put compound fertilizer as base, then urea at greening-up. Three waterings — winter water, spring water, and one at filling. Spray twice, mostly for aphids and head blight.

For summer maize after garlic, the ground is already loose so I just clear it and seed directly, no plough needed. I buy Zhengdan-style hybrid seed from the agro-shop. Fertilizer is less because garlic leftover helps. After wheat I use rotary. I irrigate twice if no rain, and spray once for the borer.

My husband helps and my son comes back for garlic harvest — that is the busy time, we hire 2-3 neighbors for a few days.
